text:
Daniil But is back with Utah after a call-up on Nov. 12, as CBS Sports reported, and the 12th overall pick from 2023 is still finding his footing at 21. He's played 17 games this season, 10.4 minutes a night, with 2 goals and 2 assists, and no goals in his last ten.

The underlying picture is kinder than the totals. Utah has held 55% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) at five on five with him on the ice, and his shooting, 11.8%, sits about where his talent range expects. Last season Evolving-Hockey liked his defense in a small sample (362 minutes): opponents got 0.13 fewer expected goals per 60 with him out there, 90th percentile. For a 6'5" winger that is an encouraging place to start.

He can move, too: 32 bursts over 20 mph this season, a lot for someone on limited minutes.

Forwards picked around him typically scored 0.37 points a game in their first full season; he's at 0.24. The minutes, not the finish, are what's holding him back so far.
